what_its_for: Olopatadine is an antihistamine eye drop used to treat itchy, red, and watery eyes caused by allergies (such as hay fever, pet dander, or dust). It works by blocking histamine, the chemical your body releases during an allergic reaction, to quickly relieve eye irritation and discomfort.
how_to_take: Wash your hands thoroughly before using. Tilt your head back and gently pull down your lower eyelid to form a small pocket. Hold the dropper above your eye without touching the eye or eyelid, and squeeze the prescribed number of drops into the pocket. Gently close your eye for 1 to 2 minutes and press lightly on the inner corner of your eye (near your nose) to prevent the medicine from draining. If you wear soft contact lenses, remove them before using the drops and wait at least 10 minutes before putting your contacts back in. If you are using more than one eye drop, wait at least 5 minutes between different eye medicines.
dosing: The usual dose depends on which product your doctor prescribed. A common dosing schedule is: Patanol (0.1%): 1 drop in each affected eye twice a day, about 6 to 8 hours apart. Pataday Once Daily Relief (0.2%): 1 drop in each affected eye once a day. Pataday Once Daily Extra Strength (0.7%) / Pazeo (0.7%): 1 drop in each affected eye once a day. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's specific instructions, as doses may vary.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not use a double dose to make up for the one you missed.
storage: Store the bottle at room temperature, between 39°F and 77°F (4°C and 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Do not freeze the eye drops. Keep out of reach of children. Discard the bottle after the expiration date printed on the label. Some products should be discarded within a certain number of days after opening — check your product label or ask your pharmacist.
what_to_avoid: Do not wear soft contact lenses while your eyes are red or irritated. Avoid touching the dropper tip to your eye, eyelid, fingers, or any other surface to prevent contamination and infection. Do not share your eye drops with anyone else. Avoid rubbing your eyes after applying the drops. Although olopatadine is not known to cause significant drowsiness like oral antihistamines, use caution driving or operating machinery until you know how this medicine affects your vision temporarily after each dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor if you experience: severe eye pain or increased eye redness after using the drops; vision changes that do not clear up quickly after applying the drops; signs of an eye infection such as discharge, crusting, or worsening redness; an allergic reaction to the medication including rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; your symptoms do not improve within a few days of starting treatment; or if your eyes become more irritated after use.
when_it_works: Olopatadine starts to relieve itching and redness fairly quickly, often within a few minutes to a couple of hours after the first dose. For best results, use it regularly as prescribed throughout allergy season or as long as your doctor recommends, even if you are feeling better.
special_populations: Children: Pataday (0.2%) and Patanol (0.1%) are generally approved for children 3 years and older. Pazeo (0.7%) is typically approved for children 2 years and older. Always confirm the correct product and dose with your child's doctor. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Your doctor will weigh the benefits and risks before recommending this medication. Older Adults: No special dose adjustments are usually needed for older adults, but always inform your doctor of all other medications and health conditions.
